answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake. Each new agent must lock collateral in a shared vault before it can trade or earn. A bridge then carries that stake into a reputation score built only from repeated, peer-attested deals. To flood the network, an attacker has to fund a separate locked deposit for every fake identity, and that capital sits idle and is slashed on fraud. Honest agents instead grow a reputation oasis that newcomers must earn or buy, so fielding a whole swarm of impostors costs far more than joining as one real member.
